correctness.rationale: Gale evenness makes each facet the union of two disjoint cycle edges, with unique such matching since a proper induced subgraph of the cycle is a union of paths. Each facet gives exactly three edges in the double, whose vertices are all pairs by neighborliness. The cycle-edge vertices a_i and a_(i+1) connect through a_(i+3), including n=5. Shortening an odd arc joins each eligible pair to this component. For even n a facet has two vertices of each parity, so no paired edge crosses the two pair types; shortening a same-parity arc stops at a length-two chord, and consecutive such chords are adjacent. The edge totals are F=n(n−3)/2 and 2F in the equal- and opposite-parity components, with vertex totals n(n−2)/4 and n²/4. These give the displayed E−V+1 values; in odd n the overall formula holds. Rotation and reflection fix each component, hence act trivially on reduced H₀.
